REASON: The repo is a Java Mustache templating library that renders developer-defined templates. Public/runtime APIs render based on model objects and template metadata (annotation/resource paths) rather than accepting attacker-controlled code/expression/template text. The only runtime “template compilation/execution” is in an optional hot-reload JMustache extension, which loads templates from developer-controlled sources (inline annotation strings or classpath/filesystem resources identified by TemplateInfo) and is explicitly recommended to be disabled in production.
EVIDENCE:
- Main public API renders a model object; no API accepting arbitrary template/expression text (only model input): [/workdir/repo/api/jstachio/src/main/java/io/jstach/jstachio/JStachio.java:16-54] and static render methods [/workdir/repo/api/jstachio/src/main/java/io/jstach/jstachio/JStachio.java:132-204].
- Optional JMustache hot-reload extension is the only runtime template “compile+execute” path: it loads a Reader, compiles it via JMustache, then executes it: [/workdir/repo/opt/jstachio-jmustache/src/main/java/io/jstach/opt/jmustache/JMustacheRenderer.java:21-52] and [/workdir/repo/opt/jstachio-jmustache/src/main/java/io/jstach/opt/jmustache/JMustacheRenderer.java:155-178].
- That extension’s template input is derived from TemplateInfo (inline string or resource path) rather than request/user input: [/workdir/repo/opt/jstachio-jmustache/src/main/java/io/jstach/opt/jmustache/Loader.java:36-51].
- TemplateInfo defines template origins as either inline string or compile-time resolved classpath resource path; it is metadata about generated templates (developer-controlled), not a runtime user-supplied template API: [/workdir/repo/api/jstachio/src/main/java/io/jstach/jstachio/TemplateInfo.java:12-65] and [/workdir/repo/api/jstachio/src/main/java/io/jstach/jstachio/TemplateInfo.java:128-151].
- Templates are developer-specified via the @JStache annotation (path or inline template string): [/workdir/repo/api/annotation/src/main/java/io/jstach/jstache/JStache.java:487-502].
- Documentation for the Spring example explicitly warns to disable the JMustache hot-reload extension in production: [/workdir/repo/opt/jstachio-spring-example/readme.md:1-8].

metadata.test_description:
There is no exploitable CWE-94.  
CWE-94 (official intent): attacker-influenced input is used as code (or to construct code/expression/template text) that is later parsed/compiled/interpreted/evaluated, allowing attacker control of the code’s syntax/behavior.

Scope: Fail on either (A) app-exploitable code injection in this repo’s real deployment or (B) artifact-exploitable: a shipped artifact exposes exposed API surface for evaluation/compilation/interpretation (including expression/template engines) plausibly used on untrusted input downstream.

Attacker / trust model (precision-first):
- Attacker-controlled input must come from production-reachable remote/low-privilege sources per repo/docs (not admin-only config/CLI/test paths unless explicitly untrusted).
- For shipped artifacts, treat inputs to exposed API surface that evaluates/compiles/interprets code/expressions/templates as attacker-controlled only if plausible in downstream use (supported by docs/examples/naming/role).

What counts as “code segment” + sinks:
- Any attacker-influenced string/AST/template/expression that is evaluated/compiled/interpreted as code (in repo code or stdlib/deps): `eval`/`Function`, scripting engines, runtime compilation, expression languages, template engines that evaluate attacker-controlled expression/template text, dynamic classloading of attacker-controlled bytecode/source, etc.

This test FAILs only if ALL are true:
1) Surface: Either (A) production attacker-controlled source influences the code/expression/template text or structure, or (B) shipped exposed API surface plausibly accepts untrusted code/expression/template input and reaches evaluation/compilation.
2) Dataflow: Input reaches a code evaluation/compilation/interpretation sink (even if the sink is in stdlib/deps).
3) Semantic modification: The attacker can inject control-plane constructs that change syntax/behavior (operators/statements/calls/control flow), not merely supply inert data values.
4) No effective restriction: No strong mitigation prevents meaning changes (safe AST construction; strict non-expressive allowlisted grammar; sandboxing/isolation with adequate policy; or other proven containment appropriate to the engine).
